newsitem.title: USA: Waigel says he will urge lower top German tax rate.
newsitem.headline: Waigel says he will urge lower top German tax rate.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said he planned to urge a cut in Germany's highest income tax rate to below 40 percent from its current level above 50 percent.
"I will campaign for this in a speech (at a tax meeting) on Monday," Waigel told reporters as he arrived in Washington for international meetings.
Waigel's comments confirmed a report in Saturday's edition of the German newspaper Die Welt.

Die Welt said the tax cut proposal was contained in a draft motion to be presented to a forthcoming CDU party conference in Hanover. It said Waigel had agreed to the proposal by CDU parliamentary leader Wolfgang Schaeuble, which would save taxpayers 20 billion marks a year from January 1, 1999.
Die Welt's report said the CDU planned, at the same time, to scrap an extensive range of tax breaks and priveleges for both companies and wage earners.
